q: What is the share of a surface that lets water soak into the ground?
n: Perviousness is the share of a surface's area that lets water soak into the ground. Source: USGBC LEED Reference Guide (definitions).

q: Ground areas that are vegetated and pervious.
n: LEED's open space is vegetated, pervious ground area on the site. Source: USGBC LEED Reference Guide (Open Space credit).

q: A precipitation that is unusually acidic.
n: Acid rain is precipitation made unusually acidic by sulfur and nitrogen oxides in the air. Source: US EPA, acid rain.

q: Which is a common source of indoor VOCs?
n: Paints, adhesives, coatings and furniture finishes are common indoor sources of VOCs (off-gassing). Source: US EPA, Indoor Air Quality; USGBC LEED (Low-Emitting Materials).

q: Which interior material has the highest embodied energy?
n: Aluminum has the highest embodied energy of the listed materials, because smelting it from bauxite is very energy-intensive. Source: Hammond & Jones, Inventory of Carbon and Energy (ICE), University of Bath.

q: Which is an alternative energy source for a building?
n: A photovoltaic (PV) system generates electricity on site, so it is an alternative (renewable) energy source. Rainwater harvesting and cool or green roofs save resources but do not generate power. Source: RA 9513 (Renewable Energy Act); RA 11285 (Energy Efficiency and Conservation Act).

q: Interms of material production and transportation, which of the following flooring materials is considered to have the lowest carbon footprint?
n: Baguio stone is a local natural stone needing little processing and short transport, so it has the lowest carbon footprint. Laminates and ceramics need energy-intensive manufacture. Source: Hammond & Jones, ICE database; USGBC LEED (regional materials).

q: What reduces heat gain in landscaping?
n: Planted ground cover cuts heat gain through shade and evapotranspiration. Dark bricks and pebble washout absorb and store heat. Source: US EPA, Heat Island Reduction; USGBC LEED.

q: Which would NOT save cost on the project?
n: Centralized air-conditioning has high first and operating costs. Daylighting, ceiling fans and local coco lumber save money. Source: RA 11285; DOE Guidelines on Energy Conserving Design of Buildings (2008).

q: What type of finish would consume less energy?
n: A plain cement finish needs no further manufactured finish material, so it has the least embodied and processing energy of the choices. Source: Hammond & Jones, ICE database.

q: Which lighting approach best cuts a building's power use?
n: Passive daylighting lights spaces with no electrical power at all, which cuts more than efficient lamps can. Source: DOE Guidelines on Energy Conserving Design of Buildings; IES Lighting Handbook.

q: Which ventilation can cut power use?
n: Natural cross ventilation moves air without fans or chillers, which cuts power use. Source: DOE Guidelines on Energy Conserving Design of Buildings; Givoni.

q: Which material should NOT be used under a strict green building ordinance?
n: Imported Italian granite carries high transport (embodied) carbon. Local coco lumber, CHB and local stone are preferred under green ordinances. Source: Quezon City Green Building Ordinance (2009); USGBC LEED (regional materials).

q: What device uses solar radiation to heat an absorber through which air or water circulates?
n: A solar collector absorbs solar radiation to heat a plate through which air or water circulates. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, HVAC Applications (solar energy use).

q: What exterior device of fixed angled fins shields a window from direct sun?
n: A sunshade or brise-soleil is an exterior device of fixed angled fins that shields windows from direct sun. Source: Olgyay, Solar Control and Shading Devices.

q: Best way to lessen noise created by traffic.
n: Tall, dense trees and planting belts are the best of the choices for buffering traffic noise. Grass, a low fence and stone pavers do little. Source: FHWA, Highway Traffic Noise (vegetation as barriers); Egan, Architectural Acoustics.

q: Which material is the most absorptive to heat?
n: Concrete has the highest heat capacity and density of the choices, so it absorbs and stores the most heat (thermal mass). Source: ASHRAE Handbook, Fundamentals (thermal properties).

q: In terms of material production, which of the following flooring materials is considered to have the lowest carbon footprint?
n: Naturally cut paver stones need only quarrying and cutting, with no kiln firing or chemical manufacture, so they have the lowest production carbon. Source: Hammond & Jones, ICE database.

q: Which fits a green design concept?
n: Rainwater collection, reuse of construction materials and waste segregation are all green practices. Source: USGBC LEED; RA 9003 (Ecological Solid Waste Management Act).

q: Which “green” practice is outright sustainable and directly beneficial to the environment?
o: Use of modular furniture and wall systems
Utilizing recyclable wall veneer to lessen VOC emissions of painting
All glass building envelope for maximum day-lighting
n: Recyclable wall veneer avoids painting and its VOC emissions, which directly benefits the environment and indoor air. Source: USGBC LEED (Low-Emitting Materials; Building Product Disclosure).

q: Which design choices add heat to a building's surroundings?
n: Reflective glass facades, air-conditioning exhaust and paved parking all add heat to the surroundings (urban heat island). Source: US EPA, Heat Island Effect.

q: Which flooring material is NOT the most economical?
n: An imported Italian granite slab is the costliest flooring choice. Local and Chinese granite tiles are cheaper. Source: Philippine construction material price data (DPWH/PSA construction materials price indices).

q: Why are LEDs preferred over other lamps?
n: LEDs are preferred because they are energy efficient, giving more lumens per watt and longer life than other lamps. Source: US DOE, Solid-State Lighting; DOE Philippines (Philippine Energy Labeling Program).

q: Which label on the refrigerator indicates that the product saves electricity?
n: Energy Star is the label for energy-efficient appliances. In the Philippines, appliances carry the PELP energy label. Source: US EPA Energy Star; DOE Philippine Energy Labeling Program.

q: "Green tag" is another name for:
n: "Green tags" is another name for renewable energy certificates (RECs), which represent the environmental attributes of renewable power. Source: US EPA, Green Power Partnership.

q: Which is NOT a natural refrigerant?
n: Freon (CFC/HCFC) refrigerants are synthetic. Natural refrigerants include hydrocarbons, ammonia, CO₂, air and water. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, Refrigeration; Montreal Protocol.

q: EER stands for:
n: EER means Energy Efficiency Ratio: cooling output in Btu/h per watt of electrical input. Source: AHRI Standard 210/240; DOE Philippines (EER labels).

q: Which is the best example of adaptive reuse?
o: Turning an old warehouse into apartments
n: Adaptive reuse gives an old building a new use, as when a warehouse is converted into apartments. Source: National Trust for Historic Preservation; Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: Which is NOT an alternative fuel?
n: Natural gas, LPG and biodiesel are alternative fuels. Coal is conventional. Source: US DOE Alternative Fuels Data Center; RA 9367 (Biofuels Act).

q: Which landscaping element best slows wind?
n: Trees used as windbreaks slow wind most effectively, over a distance of several tree heights downwind. Source: Olgyay, Design with Climate; USDA windbreak guidance.

q: Which landscaping element best cuts glare outdoors?
n: Dense tree canopies shade surfaces and cut glare outdoors. Reflective paving increases it. Source: Olgyay, Design with Climate; IES.

q: Which is NOT a green building strategy?
n: High-VOC finishes harm indoor air quality, so they are not a green strategy. Source: USGBC LEED (Low-Emitting Materials).
